rolesTable.reading: The 14 dead/null-session 404s are LEGION-6 ×6, LEGION-9 ×5 (all but its architect) and 3 never-claimed null tokens; 6 + 5 = 11 = `reaped=11`, so the new image's single non-zero reaper cycle removed exactly the claims of dead holders and no live one. All 31 live-session 404s were heartbeating 2–3 times inside 13:27:31–13:33:00 (so `isAlive` was true at 13:32:31) and there is no later non-zero reaper cycle, no self-health rebuild, and the 13:59 storm lasted ~70 s (< the 5-min session-cache TTL) — no evidence the NEW image dropped a live holder's claim. Their claims were therefore lost before 13:27:23 on the old image (fcd13a14: interest `Reap()`→`Remove()`→`releaseAllRoleClaims` on any KV read error, Part A path (b)) or via the unlogged read-path `ReleaseExpiredRoleClaim`; the old container's log is gone (container recreated), so the moment is unrecoverable. acceptance6.distinctListenerFinding: None proven against the new image (15d92603): the one reap it performed removed dead holders only. Observation for the Envoy owner: the restore grace is `time.Since(openedAt) < sessionTTL` and the reaper's first tick is at exactly `interval == sessionTTL`, so a restored claim whose holder has not re-registered by then has zero margin — harmless while heartbeats (120 s) are well inside 5 min.
